_help: Warm-up sentences: one error each. 'wrong' must appear exactly once in 'text'. Keep at least 5 per code. Codes must match data/codes.json.

items.text: Yesterday I meet my tutor to discuss my essay.
items.explanation: Yesterday is a finished time, so use the past simple. Meet is irregular: met.

items.text: The company has been founded in 1998.
items.explanation: In 1998 is a finished time, so use the past simple passive: was founded.

items.text: Since 2020, the number of online courses grew quickly.
items.explanation: Since 2020 connects the past to now, so use the present perfect: has grown.

items.text: When I was at school, I study French for three years.
items.explanation: When I was at school is finished time, so use the past simple: studied.

items.text: House prices rise sharply last year.
items.explanation: Last year is a finished time. Rise is irregular: rose.

items.text: I live in Brisbane since January.
items.explanation: Since January connects the past to now, so use the present perfect: have lived.

items.text: She has wrote two reports this month.
items.explanation: After has, use the past participle. Write, wrote, written.

items.text: We are plan a group presentation.
items.explanation: After are, use the -ing form: are planning.

items.text: I am looking forward to meet you.
items.explanation: In look forward to, to is a preposition, so the -ing form follows: meeting.

items.text: The results were analyse by the research team.
items.explanation: In the passive, use be + past participle: were analysed.

items.text: He wants improving his writing.
items.explanation: After want, use to + verb: wants to improve.

items.text: She did not came to the lecture.
items.explanation: After did or did not, use the base verb: did not come.

items.text: The number of students have increased.
items.explanation: The main noun is number (singular), so use has.

items.text: Everyone in my class speak two languages.
items.explanation: Everyone is singular, so the verb needs -s: speaks.

items.text: One of my friends live in Perth.
items.explanation: The subject is one (singular), not friends, so use lives.

items.text: Each student need a library card.
items.explanation: Each + singular noun takes a singular verb: needs.

items.text: My parents works in a hospital.
items.explanation: Parents is plural, so the verb has no -s: work.

items.text: Mathematics are my favourite subject.
items.explanation: Mathematics looks plural but is one subject, so use is.

items.text: She is engineer at a large company.
items.explanation: Jobs need a or an: she is an engineer. Use an before a vowel sound.

items.text: I would like to become doctor.
items.explanation: A singular countable noun needs an article: a doctor.

items.text: This is best restaurant in the city.
items.explanation: Superlatives need the: the best.

items.text: Sun rises in the east.
items.explanation: There is only one sun, so we use the: The sun.

items.text: Can you give me an information about the course?
items.explanation: Information is uncountable, so it never takes a or an.

items.text: We visited the Canberra last year.
items.explanation: City names do not take the: Canberra.

items.text: I have three sister.
items.explanation: After three, use a plural noun: sisters.

items.text: There are many advantage of studying online.
items.explanation: After many, use a plural countable noun: advantages.

items.text: She gave me some useful advices.
items.explanation: Advice is uncountable, so it has no plural form.

items.text: Two woman won the prize.
items.explanation: Woman has an irregular plural: women.

items.text: One of my friend is a nurse.
items.explanation: One of is followed by a plural noun: one of my friends.

items.text: We bought some new furnitures for the flat.
items.explanation: Furniture is uncountable, so it has no plural form.

items.text: I am interested on psychology.
items.explanation: Interested goes with in: interested in.

items.text: The lecture starts on 9 am.
items.explanation: Use at with clock times: at 9 am.

items.text: She arrived to Sydney last night.
items.explanation: Use arrive in with cities and countries, and arrive at with buildings. Not arrive to.

items.text: This book is very different with the film.
items.explanation: Different goes with from (or to in Australian and British English), not with.

items.text: We discussed the problem in Monday.
items.explanation: Use on with days: on Monday.

items.text: He is very good in maths.
items.explanation: Good goes with at for skills: good at maths.

items.text: She speaks English very good.
items.explanation: To describe how someone speaks, use the adverb well, not the adjective good.

items.text: The economic of Australia is strong.
items.explanation: After the and before of, use a noun: the economy.

items.text: It was a very interested lecture.
items.explanation: The lecture causes the feeling, so use interesting. People feel interested.

items.text: He checks his work careful.
items.explanation: To describe how he checks, use the adverb carefully.

items.text: There is a strongly link between sleep and memory.
items.explanation: Before a noun, use an adjective: a strong link.

items.text: We need to improvement our results.
items.explanation: After to, use a verb: to improve.

items.text: I need to do a decision about my course.
items.explanation: We make a decision, not do a decision.

items.text: Please say me the answer.
items.explanation: We tell someone something. We say something (to someone).

items.text: The rent in Sydney is very expensive.
items.explanation: Rent and prices are high or low. Things you buy are expensive.

items.text: I made a lot of research for this essay.
items.explanation: We do research, not make research.

items.text: Can you borrow me your pen?
items.explanation: You lend something to someone. You borrow something from someone.

items.text: The lecturer learned us how to write a summary.
items.explanation: A teacher teaches (taught) students. Students learn.

items.text: Can you tell me where is the library?
items.explanation: In a question inside a sentence, use statement order: where the library is.

items.text: She speaks very well English.
items.explanation: Do not put words between a verb and its object: speaks English very well.

items.text: I often am late for class.
items.explanation: Put often after be: am often late.

items.text: He bought a car red.
items.explanation: In English, adjectives go before the noun: a red car.

items.text: I don't know what does this word mean.
items.explanation: In a question inside a sentence, use statement order and no does: what this word means.

items.text: They visited last year Japan.
items.explanation: Put the object right after the verb, and the time at the end: visited Japan last year.

items.text: Its a difficult question.
items.explanation: It's means it is. Its shows that something belongs to it.

items.text: The dog wagged it's tail.
items.explanation: The tail belongs to the dog, so use its with no apostrophe.

items.text: The students book was on the desk.
items.explanation: Use an apostrophe to show who owns something: the student's book.

items.text: However the results were clear.
items.explanation: Put a comma after However at the start of a sentence.

items.text: Where is the library.
items.explanation: A direct question ends with a question mark.

items.text: In addition students need a laptop.
items.explanation: Put a comma after linking phrases such as In addition at the start of a sentence.

items.text: I was tired, I went to bed early.
items.explanation: Do not join two full sentences with only a comma. Use so, a full stop or a semicolon.

items.text: Because it was raining. We stayed inside.
items.explanation: A because clause cannot be a sentence on its own. Join it to the main clause with a comma.

items.text: Although I studied hard, but I failed the test.
items.explanation: Use although or but, not both.

items.text: Many students who live on campus.
items.explanation: This sentence has no main verb. Remove who so that live becomes the main verb.

items.text: There are many people want to study abroad.
items.explanation: Two verbs (are, want) need a joining word: people who want.

items.text: I like reading, it helps me relax.
items.explanation: Do not join two full sentences with only a comma. Use because, a full stop or a semicolon.

items.text: She very tired after the exam.
items.explanation: Every sentence needs a verb. Add was before the adjective.

items.text: Is important to sleep well.
items.explanation: English sentences need a subject. Add it: It is important.

items.text: My brother twenty years old.
items.explanation: Use be with age: my brother is twenty years old.

items.text: Students not allowed to eat in the library.
items.explanation: The sentence needs a verb. Use are with not allowed.

items.text: I look forward hearing from you.
items.explanation: The phrase is look forward to + -ing.

items.text: He asked me I could help him.
items.explanation: Reported yes/no questions need if or whether.

items.text: We discussed about the plan.
items.explanation: We discuss something. Do not add about.

items.text: My brother he works in Perth.
items.explanation: Use one subject only: my brother works, not my brother he works.

items.text: I want to return back home.
items.explanation: Return already means go back, so back is not needed.

items.text: She married with a doctor.
items.explanation: We marry someone. Do not add with.

items.text: This method is more better than the old one.
items.explanation: Better already means more good, so more is not needed.

items.text: Please contact to the office.
items.explanation: We contact someone. Do not add to.

items.text: Many child in my class speak Arabic.
items.explanation: Child has an irregular plural: children.

items.text: We need two box for these books.
items.explanation: After two, use a plural noun. Nouns ending in -x add -es: boxes.

items.text: I go to the work by bus every day.
items.explanation: In go to work, work means your job or workplace and has no article.

items.text: The lab has some new equipments.
items.explanation: Equipment is uncountable, so it has no plural form.

items.text: There is a lot of researches on this topic.
items.explanation: Research is uncountable, so it has no plural form.

items.text: How many money do you need for the trip?
items.explanation: Money is uncountable, so use much, not many.

items.text: The library is open late. Especially during exams.
items.explanation: Especially during exams is not a full sentence. Join it to the sentence before.

items.text: I moved to Sydney in 2022. To study engineering.
items.explanation: To study engineering is not a full sentence. Join it to the sentence before.

items.text: We stayed home all weekend. Because of the storm.
items.explanation: Because of the storm is not a full sentence. Join it to the sentence before.

items.text: The results were clear. Which surprised us.
items.explanation: A which clause cannot be a sentence on its own. Join it to the sentence before with a comma.

items.text: It was raining, we stayed inside.
items.explanation: Do not join two full sentences with only a comma. Use so, a full stop or a semicolon.

items.text: The test was easy, everyone passed.
items.explanation: Do not join two full sentences with only a comma. Use so, a full stop or a semicolon.
